ai.description: This slender lizard reaches 55 cm. It is bright green with a distinct, spiny crest along the neck and back. A dark patch often surrounds the eye and ear.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Bronchocela jubata* is uniquely identified by the prominent, elongated, sickle-shaped scales forming a distinct crest along the nape, which are much larger than in other species.
ai.habitat: The maned forest lizard inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests, often found in canopy foliage and shrubbery at low to moderate elevations across the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The maned forest lizard is primarily diurnal, often seen basking on tree trunks or branches to regulate its body temperature before actively foraging for insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Bronchocela jubata* is oviparous, laying clutches of 2–9 eggs in soil. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, peaking between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Bronchocela jubata* is found in the Nicobar Islands of India, typically inhabiting lowland tropical forests and coastal vegetation at low elevations.
